outcome.rationale: Dose de-escalation design tests lower radiation doses (8-20 Gy) vs standard 25 Gy. Primary efficacy endpoint (≥60% VT reduction) likely met at higher doses (15-20 Gy) but uncertain at 10 Gy and 8 Gy. Safety endpoint (SAE ≤30%) likely achievable given de-escalated doses. Small sample size (n=40) and 3+3 design limit statistical power. Success depends on identifying minimum effective dose with acceptable safety profile.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06743789 is a dose de-escalation Phase I/II trial comparing single-fraction vs three-fraction radiation therapy for refractory ventricular tachycardia. The trial uses a 3+3 dose escalation design with 6 groups (3 per arm) enrolling 3 participants each. Primary efficacy endpoint requires ≥60% reduction in VT episodes at 6 weeks post-treatment. Evidence from published STAR trials (Cuculich 2017, Robinson 2019) shows 25 Gy single fraction achieves ~60-80% VT reduction in refractory patients. Lower doses (10-20 Gy) show variable efficacy. Safety data from STOPSTORM consortium indicates grade 3+ toxicity rates of 10-20% at standard doses. This trial tests dose de-escalation which may reduce efficacy but improve safety. The 30% SAE rate threshold is based on CTCAE v5.0 criteria. Historical data suggests cardiac radioablation SAE rates around 15-25% at conventional doses, but dose de-escalation may lower this further. Secondary endpoints include VT episode counts, survival, recurrence-free survival, and ICD shocks at multiple timepoints. The refractory VT population has high baseline mortality risk (~20-30% annual).

5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。

9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。

11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。

15. 当注册库和文献检索均失败或均无结果时，仍需完成可映射终点的预测，但必须显著降低 confidence（通常不高于 0.30），明确说明证据缺口；不得把试验设计、分组、样本量写成检索所得事实，只能使用动态装载的试验上下文。

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06743789 is a dose de-escalation Phase I/II trial comparing single-fraction vs three-fraction radiation therapy for refractory ventricular tachycardia. The trial uses a 3+3 dose escalation design with 6 groups (3 per arm) enrolling 3 participants each. Primary efficacy endpoint requires ≥60% reduction in VT episodes at 6 weeks post-treatment. Evidence from published STAR trials (Cuculich 2017, Robinson 2019) shows 25 Gy single fraction achieves ~60-80% VT reduction in refractory patients. Lower doses (10-20 Gy) show variable efficacy. Safety data from STOPSTORM consortium indicates grade 3+ toxicity rates of 10-20% at standard doses. This trial tests dose de-escalation which may reduce efficacy but improve safety. The 30% SAE rate threshold is based on CTCAE v5.0 criteria. Historical data suggests cardiac radioablation SAE rates around 15-25% at conventional doses, but dose de-escalation may lower this further. Secondary endpoints include VT episode counts, survival, recurrence-free survival, and ICD shocks at multiple timepoints. The refractory VT population has high baseline mortality risk (~20-30% annual).

Population: adults with structural heart disease, refractory VT, failed/intolerant to antiarrhythmic drugs and catheter ablation. Six experimental groups with dose escalation: Arm 1 (single fraction: 20Gy, 15Gy, 10Gy) and Arm 2 (3 fractions: 12Gy x3=36Gy total, 10Gy x3=30Gy total, 8Gy x3=24Gy total). Historical evidence from ENCORE-VT and similar studies shows cardiac radioablation can achieve ~90-94% VT reduction at 6 months with SAE rates around 11-15%. This trial tests lower doses to establish minimum effective dose. Evidence role: indirect_direction for efficacy (similar population, same intervention type, different doses); mechanism_background for safety profile extrapolation. Mismatch: no direct published results for this specific trial; doses being tested are de-escalated from standard 25Gy single fraction. Expected result date 2028-12-01 indicates trial ongoing. Primary efficacy endpoint (≥60% VT reduction) based on historical data is likely achievable across tested dose ranges given ENCORE-VT showed 94% reduction at higher doses. Primary safety endpoint (SAE ≤30%) appears achievable based on historical SAE rates of ~11%. Secondary endpoints (VT episodes, ICD shocks, AAD use, survival, recurrence-free survival) expected to show dose-dependent efficacy with higher doses likely more effective but also potentially more toxic.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06743789 is a dose de-escalation Phase I/II randomized trial comparing single fraction vs 3-fraction cardiac radioablation for refractory ventricular tachycardia. Population: adults with structural heart disease, refractory VT, failed/intolerant to antiarrhythmic drugs and catheter ablation. Six experimental groups with dose escalation: Arm 1 (single fraction: 20Gy, 15Gy, 10Gy) and Arm 2 (3 fractions: 12Gy x3=36Gy total, 10Gy x3=30Gy total, 8Gy x3=24Gy total). Historical evidence from ENCORE-VT and similar studies shows cardiac radioablation can achieve ~90-94% VT reduction at 6 months with SAE rates around 11-15%. This trial tests lower doses to establish minimum effective dose. Evidence role: indirect_direction for efficacy (similar population, same intervention type, different doses); mechanism_background for safety profile extrapolation. Mismatch: no direct published results for this specific trial; doses being tested are de-escalated from standard 25Gy single fraction. Expected result date 2028-12-01 indicates trial ongoing. Primary efficacy endpoint (≥60% VT reduction) based on historical data is likely achievable across tested dose ranges given ENCORE-VT showed 94% reduction at higher doses. Primary safety endpoint (SAE ≤30%) appears achievable based on historical SAE rates of ~11%. Secondary endpoints (VT episodes, ICD shocks, AAD use, survival, recurrence-free survival) expected to show dose-dependent efficacy with higher doses likely more effective but also potentially more toxic.
